criteria.title: Select one actual operating business
criteria.action: Record business identity, service types, crew size, operator contact, operating timezone and its current system. List required integrations and any payroll or inventory dependency.
criteria.acceptance: The selected service matches the operator's actual daily route; each unusual dependency has a named treatment in the agreed scope.
criteria.retain: Business profile, dependency list and selected scope.

criteria.title: Keep published terms and the selected agreement distinct
criteria.action: Record links, retrieval dates and draft labels beside the agreement actually selected for this pilot. Record who selected it and when setup work begins.
criteria.acceptance: The desk can display the source version separately from the operator's agreed scope, dates and commercial treatment. An unresolved source detail stays visible as a question assigned to its actual owner.
criteria.retain: Source register, agreement reference, setup-start event and open questions.

criteria.title: Record the actual service and usage basis
criteria.action: Enter the selected setup/monthly amounts, billing start, usage responsibility and payment-account owner. Preserve a later negotiated amount beside the published reference.
criteria.acceptance: The operating budget separates software, SMS and card costs and identifies whose account receives customer payments.
criteria.retain: Selected commercial record and usage-cost owner.

criteria.title: Configure the operator's identity and service catalogue
criteria.action: Load the agreed name, logo, domain, services, prices, taxes, service area and booking rules from the intake.
criteria.acceptance: One authored booking displays the selected operator identity and service details consistently through the invoice and customer document.
criteria.retain: Configuration export and the authored booking reference.

criteria.title: Retain the original export before mapping
criteria.action: Receive the operator-authorized original files, inventory every file and count records by entity. Preserve original bytes and timestamps before any transformations.
criteria.acceptance: Every received file remains available and is attributable to one intake; corrections are separate editions with a stated reason.
criteria.retain: Original-file manifest, row counts and intake owner.

criteria.title: Make each field and relationship explicit
criteria.action: Map source identifiers, customer/property relationships, visits, invoice amounts/statuses and dates. Record timezone, currency and duplicate rules. Keep exceptions assigned to an operator.
criteria.acceptance: Every in-scope source field is mapped, intentionally retained as extra information or explicitly excluded; customer/job/invoice references remain connected.
criteria.retain: Complete mapping, duplicate decisions and unresolved-source list.

criteria.title: Reconcile operational and financial continuity
criteria.action: Compare imported counts, future appointments, outstanding balances and paid/void states to the original export. Resolve missing links and unexpected differences within the same case.
criteria.acceptance: Booked work and invoice balances can be traced to the received source; every remaining difference has a documented operator decision.
criteria.retain: Before/after reconciliation and the complete exception decisions.

criteria.title: Plan the changeover from the still-running system
criteria.action: Choose a cutover window, identify records created or changed during preparation, and name the responsible operator for the final delta and fallback.
criteria.acceptance: The plan accounts for new bookings and payments through the selected switch time, with a way to resume the original process if the cutover is deferred.
criteria.retain: Cutover worksheet, delta inventory and fallback contact.

criteria.title: Give the operator an individual account
criteria.action: Use the intended owner identity in the selected private instance. Exercise ordinary sign-in, sign-out and the supported recovery path during the walkthrough.
criteria.acceptance: The owner can return to the intended business workspace through its normal entry point; credentials are kept out of the desk and shared documents.
criteria.retain: Instance URL, named account custodian and walkthrough result.

criteria.title: Review the actual technician role
criteria.action: With an operator-authorized technician account, open its normal day view and one same-day invoice. In the same workflow inspect the owner-only routes the operator depends on.
criteria.acceptance: The observed role fits the published daily-work boundary; any broader access is recorded against the exact route for the product owner to correct.
criteria.retain: Role matrix and actual route/result notes.

criteria.title: Record system and provider custody
criteria.action: Name the business owner and technical custodian of the instance, domain, data store, email, messaging and payment connections. Record references and recovery contacts without secrets.
criteria.acceptance: The operator can identify who controls each connection and where customer data belongs; a handover does not require a password embedded in a document.
criteria.retain: Account-custody register and recovery contacts.

criteria.title: Operate a booking through the selected rules
criteria.action: Use an authored pilot customer and the configured public booking route; carry the booking into the schedule, visit and final invoice on the operator's phone.
criteria.acceptance: The intended service, time, address and selected charges remain consistent through the operator's normal day.
criteria.retain: One linked booking-to-invoice course and reviewed phone/desktop views.

criteria.title: Carry consent with the contact
criteria.action: For controlled pilot contacts, record consent source, scope, wording/version and time. Make absent or limited consent visible before enabling communications.
criteria.acceptance: Only the communication appropriate to the recorded scope is selected; a service contact is not silently reclassified as a marketing subscriber.
criteria.retain: Contact permission record and selected communication purpose.

criteria.title: Join the actual business messaging connection
criteria.action: Retain the provider's actual number/registration result and responsible custodian. Use a consenting operator-controlled contact for a send and reply in the private pilot instance.
criteria.acceptance: The chosen business sender and reply appear in the intended conversation; registration status is an observed provider result.
criteria.retain: Nonsecret registration reference, sender identity and message result.

criteria.title: Continue the same conversation through an opt-out
criteria.action: Use the controlled contact's opt-out in the selected pilot course, then inspect its recorded communication preference before the next queued or manual action.
criteria.acceptance: The contact's new preference is retained and reflected in subsequent messaging decisions; the course records the actual observed result.
criteria.retain: Opt-out event and subsequent communication disposition.

criteria.title: Select automation with the operator
criteria.action: Identify the actual triggers enabled for the authored course, their recipient, timing and owner. Review the resulting customer copy before a selected trigger is exercised.
criteria.acceptance: Each enabled action has an intentional recipient and observable result; repeated operating actions do not leave unexplained repeated customer messages.
criteria.retain: Selected automation list and linked delivery results.

criteria.title: Connect the operator-owned payment account
criteria.action: Record the operator's chosen Stripe connection and use its supported test or operator-approved pilot flow; follow the hosted payment link through to the invoice result.
criteria.acceptance: Payment belongs to the selected business account and reconciles to one invoice; the desk retains reference/status/amount rather than card details.
criteria.retain: Payment-account custody, invoice reference and reconciliation.

criteria.title: Reconcile a corrected or incomplete payment state
criteria.action: Select a relevant failed, reversed or manually recorded payment path with the operator. Preserve the original event and the correcting event together.
criteria.acceptance: The resulting amount due and customer document match the selected payment history without discarding the original invoice.
criteria.retain: Original payment history, correction and resulting customer document.

criteria.title: Receive each promised self-serve export
criteria.action: From the selected instance, download the available self-serve entity exports and inventory their columns, counts, timestamps and source view.
criteria.acceptance: The recipient opens the actual files and reconciles the selected pilot records to the operating workspace.
criteria.retain: Export manifest, original files and receiving notes.

criteria.title: Account for the full handover scope
criteria.action: Build a coverage matrix for every agreed entity, relationship, document and attachment. Mark whether each comes from self-service, a supplied export or another agreed path.
criteria.acceptance: Every item in the selected handover has a real received output or a specifically assigned missing-output action; a smaller CSV set is not labeled complete.
criteria.retain: Coverage matrix, missing-output ownership and received handover.

criteria.title: Reopen the same records from the delivered files
criteria.action: Open the handover in a clean receiving workspace using the agreed destination, retaining original identifiers. Follow one customer's linked job, invoice, payment and communication through the received records.
criteria.acceptance: The recipient can use the delivered information without the originating browser session, and exceptions remain connected to their source.
criteria.retain: Receiving result, relationships and unresolved items.

criteria.title: Document the operator's selected exit treatment
criteria.action: Record the effective cancellation date, final billing, export destination and any agreed retention. Keep active-system removal and backup expiry as separate fields; preserve unset values when not established.
criteria.acceptance: The plan states what will happen and who owns it using the selected agreement and actual provider information.
criteria.retain: Exit plan, agreement reference and backup-retention source.

criteria.title: Let the operator complete the working course
criteria.action: Have the operator use the saved pilot on the phone: find today's job, review access notes, continue the visit, invoice, receive a reply and locate its export. Open the same record on desktop.
criteria.acceptance: The operator can resume the saved work through the normal entry points and identify how to obtain support.
criteria.retain: Completed course, usable guide and assigned follow-up work.

criteria.title: Review the actual operator package
criteria.action: Review the outgoing guide, selected terms, screenshots and downloadable files as the operator will receive them. Keep private customer data out of the public sandbox and internal delivery destinations out of customer instructions.
criteria.acceptance: The delivered package is readable, current and opens from its actual recipient-facing surface; the public/demo policy scope is not silently applied to the private instance.
criteria.retain: Final package edition, image review and recipient-ready handover.
